driver_archetypes.rationale: Compliant car baseline. High tau and tight minGap ensure cars stop at red (M2/early/car ~0) and maintain low discharge headway (M1/car).
Car violators (custom2) drawn from 'car' distribution; currently compliant (p=0) to match M3/share/car low red-running.

Compliant motorcycle baseline. Share adjusted to 0.6 (with moto_seeker at 0.4) summing to 1.0 for the 'moto' distribution. minGap=1.9m is wide to prevent overshoot in this archetype, relying on rule-triggered behavior for M4/overshoot.

Motorcycle violators drawing from the 'moto' distribution. Share increased to 0.4 to boost wrong-lane usage probability (M8/moto target ~0.21) and early-start frequency (M2/early/moto). Identical physical params to moto_saval but enabled for queue_space_seeking rules.
Illegal left-turning motorcycles (distribution moto_violator); share 1.0 ensures the 'moto_violator' distribution sums to exactly 1.0, retaining jmTimegapMinor for box-waiting mechanics.

traci_rules.rationale: Matches Saval et al. 2023 Sec 4 (front-row motorcycle red-running probability ~0.5); k=0 removes swarm effect; targets M3/share/moto by providing the base probability for red-light running.

Targets M2/early/moto (observed share 0.1303). Increasing p from 0.0 to 0.13 allows a significant portion of front-row motorcycles to creep over the stop line in the last seconds of red, directly addressing the large underestimation observed in previous iterations.

Targets M8/moto wrong-lane share (observed 0.2131). Since 'moto_seeker' has a share of 0.4 in the total motorcycle demand, setting p_wrong_lane=0.42 yields an effective usage probability roughly matching the observation when combined with other factors. t_g_s=7s estimates green clearance to trigger behaviour before the light turns green.
Field observation: most motorcycles pass a standing U-turner; p=0.8 (80% probability) and t_wait=2s reflects quick lateral filtering.
Field observation: cars rarely bypass standing U-turners; p=0.1 (10% probability) matches conservative car behaviour.
